title: Quickstart
description: Your first routed request in under five minutes.
content:
Prism is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If your code talks to OpenAI today, changing two lines makes it talk to every model in the pool.

1. Get a key

Create a key in the dashboard. Keys are scoped to a project and carry their own budget, rate limit and default policy.

2. Point your client at Prism

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.prism.example/v1",
    api_key="pk_live_…",
)

reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="prism/auto",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this transcript…"}],
)

The model id prism/auto hands the choice to your key's default policy. Any catalog id — anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, say — pins that model and the router steps aside.

3. Read the log

Every response carries an x-prism-route header naming the model that answered and the policy that chose it. The same record, with cost and latency, is in the dashboard within a second.

Next

Write a routing policy, turn on fallbacks, and set a budget on the key before it goes to production.

title: Routing policies
description: Route by cost, speed, quality or context — in a file you can commit.
content:
A policy is an ordered list of rules. The first rule whose when matches decides the model; if none match, the default rule does.

Shape

name: production
rules:
  - when: task == "summarize"
    then: cheapest_above(quality: 80)
  - when: context_tokens > 400_000
    then: model("google/gemini-3.1-pro")
  - when: p95_latency > 800ms
    then: fallback_next
default: best_quality(max_input_price: 5.00)

Selectors

SelectorPicks
cheapest_above(quality)The lowest blended price with a score at or above the floor
fastest(within_quality)The lowest p50 first-token latency within N points of the best score
best_quality(max_input_price)The highest score that costs no more than the cap
longest_contextThe largest context window in the pool
model(id)Exactly that model

Task detection

The task field is inferred from the request unless you set the x-prism-task header. Detection is a small classifier that runs in the router, adds under a millisecond, and is logged so you can check it.

Committing policies

Policies are YAML. Keep them in your repo and push with prism policies push; the dashboard editor reads and writes the same format.

title: Fallbacks and retries
description: Automatic retries across providers when one degrades, including mid-stream.
content:
Fallbacks are on by default for every policy. A request that fails, times out or lands in a degraded provider region is retried on the next eligible model in the same call.

What counts as degraded

  • A 5xx or 429 from the provider
  • First-token latency above the policy's threshold for a two-minute window
  • An error rate above 2% in the same window

Degradation is measured per provider region across all Prism traffic, so a region can be skipped before your own requests hit it.

Streaming

When a stream drops, the router resumes the completion on the next model with the tokens already delivered as context. The client sees one stream. The log records two legs, each with its own cost.

Limits

A request is retried at most three times. Each retry counts against the key's rate limit. Set fallbacks: off in the policy to disable them for a rule, or send x-prism-fallbacks: off per request.

Recovery

A recovered region is ramped back — 1%, 10%, then 100% of eligible traffic — over roughly ten minutes as long as its numbers hold.

title: Usage and limits
description: Per-key budgets, rate limits, spend alerts and the usage export.
content:
Every key carries a budget and a rate limit. Both are enforced in the router before a request reaches a provider, so an overrun never becomes a surprise invoice.

Budgets

Set a daily or monthly cap in dollars. At 50, 80 and 100 percent the key fires an alert to email or a webhook. At 100 percent you choose: hard-stop with a 402, or downgrade to the fast tier and keep serving.

Rate limits

Requests per minute and tokens per minute, per key. Prism's own limits are additive to each provider's; when a provider limit is the binding one, the router spreads load across providers before it returns a 429.

The usage view

Spend, tokens and requests by model, key, policy and day. Every number in the dashboard is also a row in the export: GET /v1/usage?from=…&to=…&group=model returns CSV or JSON.
